update_log: Baseline initialization of frequently tested sports terminology and jargon used in major domestic and international games for Sports Static GK.

cricket.description: A delivery bowled by a right-arm leg-spin bowler that spins in the opposite direction to a normal leg-spin.
An over consisting of six deliveries in which no runs are scored by the batsman.
A method of dismissal where the ball strikes the batsman's body (usually the leg) before the bat, and would have gone on to hit the stumps.
A fielding position placed very close to the batsman on the off-side.
A delivery pitched right at the batsman's toes or the base of the stumps.

football_and_hockey.description: A rule violation that occurs when an attacking player receives the ball while being closer to the opponent's goal line than both the ball and the second-last defender.
A penalty awarded against the defending team for an infringement in the penalty circle.
A method used to restart the game after a stoppage caused by an injury or an accidental breach of rules.
Shown by the referee to indicate that a player is sent off the field for a serious foul or for receiving a second yellow card.

tennis_and_badminton.description: A score of 40-all in a game, meaning a player must win two consecutive points to win the game.
A legal serve that is not touched by the receiver, winning the point for the server.
A call that requires the point to be replayed, usually because a serve hits the net but still lands in the correct service box.
A term used to represent a score of zero.
A softly hit shot that drops abruptly just over the net, meant to catch the opponent off guard.

golf.description: A score of one stroke under par on a hole.
A score of one stroke over par on a hole.
A score of two strokes under par on a hole.
A score of three strokes under par on a hole (extremely rare).
A small peg placed in the ground to elevate the ball for the first stroke of a hole.

boxing_and_wrestling.description: A punch thrown upward at the opponent's chin.
A stance used by a left-handed boxer, leading with the right hand and right foot.
A wrestling hold where one arm is passed under the opponent's arm from behind and applied to the neck.
